en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Section on the Puzzling Questions, Chapter on the Knowledge of Omniscience.
1. The Question on the Ripening of the Deeds of Supernormal Power “Venerable Nāgasena, this was said by the Blessed One:
‘Monks, this is the foremost among my disciples, monks, who possess supernormal power: namely, Mahāmoggallāna.’”
Furthermore, it is said that he was beaten with clubs until his head was split open, his bones, flesh, and veins were crushed and severed, and he attained final Nibbāna.
"Venerable Nāgasena, if the Elder Mahāmoggallāna had reached the pinnacle of psychic power (*iddhi*), then the statement that he attained final Nibbāna after being beaten with clubs must be false.
If he attained final Nibbāna after being beaten with clubs, then the statement that he had reached the pinnacle of psychic power must also be false."
“Is he not capable of removing his own injury by means of psychic power (iddhi), and is he not worthy to become a refuge even for the world with its devas?
This too is a dilemma from both sides that has come to you; it must be resolved by you.
“This too, Great King, was spoken by the Blessed One:”
“Bhikkhus, this is the foremost among my disciples, the bhikkhus who possess psychic power: namely, Mahāmoggallāna.
Yet the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna passed away after being struck by a club, and that was due to the obsession of his own past karma.
“But, venerable Nāgasena, are not both the range of psychic power of one possessing psychic power and the ripening of karma unthinkable? And should the unthinkable be removed by the unthinkable?”
“Venerable sir, just as some who desire fruit strike a wood-apple with a wood-apple, or strike a mango with a mango;
even so, venerable Nāgasena, having struck the inconceivable with the inconceivable, it should be removed.
“Even among inconceivable things, O Great King, one is superior and more powerful than the others.”
"Just as, Great King, there may be kings upon the earth who are of equal birth, yet among those of equal birth, one alone overcomes all others and exercises authority;
even so, Great King, among those inconceivable factors, it is the ripening of karma (*kamma-vipāka*) alone that is preeminent and more powerful.
It is the ripening of karma alone that overcomes all others and exercises authority; for one who is seized by karma, the remaining activities find no opportunity."
Moreover, Great King, suppose some man should offend against someone in a certain matter;
neither his mother, nor his father, nor his sister, nor his brothers, nor his friends, nor his companions can protect him;
rather, it is the king alone who, having overcome the situation there, issues his command.
What is the reason for that?
It is their state of having committed an offense.
In the very same way, Great King, among those inconceivable things, it is the ripening of karma alone that is preeminent and more powerful.
It exercises its power by overcoming all else, even the ripening of karma; for one who is seized by karma, no other remaining activities find an opportunity.

Or again, Great King, just as when a forest fire has broken out on the earth, even a thousand pots of water cannot extinguish it, but the fire alone overcomes everything there and exercises its power.
What is the reason for this?
As fire prevails over the strong,
even so, Great King, among those inconceivable things, it is the ripening of karma alone that is most preeminent and powerful;
the ripening of karma alone prevails by overcoming all else and exercises its command, while all other activities are merely subordinate to one who is seized by karma.
“They find no opportunity; therefore, Great King, when the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna was seized by his karma and beaten with clubs, he had no application of psychic power.
“Excellent, Bhante Nāgasena! So it is; thus do I accept it.”
The first question on the ripening of kamma through supernormal power.
